articles.title: Experts: One-China principle unshakable, 'Taiwan independence' doomed
articles.titleCn: 专家：一个中国原则不可动摇，“台独”注定失败
articles.summary: The recent meeting between the heads of state of China and the United States and the China-Russia-US summit have sent a clear message: the Taiwan question is at the heart of China's core interests and the international community's commitment to the one-China principle is unshakable, experts and scholars across the Taiwan Strait said.
articles.summaryCn: 中美俄领导人会晤及特朗普表态不支持“台独”，再次表明一个中国原则不可撼动，专家指出“台独”分裂行径注定失败。

They said the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces and military {{4}} are {{1}} to fail. On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping met with US President Donald Trump, who was in the southern Chinese metropolis of Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. Xi also hosted a historic summit with Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the same day. During his meeting with Trump, Xi said that on the Taiwan question, the US side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major {{5}} in China-US relations.

Li said Taiwan's restoration to China was one of the outcomes of victory in World War II and an important part of the postwar international order, adding that the historical and legal fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China is clear and {{25}}. By recalling the three countries' history of fighting side by side during World War II and reaffirming their commitment to safeguarding the postwar international order and the purposes of the UN Charter, the summit sent a stern warning to forces seeking to challenge that order and undermine the achievements of the war, including secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," she said. Feng Wang, a Taiwan-based history writer, said the history of World War II and the victory over fascism were shared historical memories of the international community that must neither be forgotten nor distorted. People in Taiwan should not be misled by political manipulation or erroneous views of history, Wang said, adding that people from all walks of life in Taiwan should take a long-term and broad view, thinking in the direction that benefits Taiwan compatriots, the country and the Chinese nation.

articles.fullText:
The recent meeting between the heads of state of China and the United States and the China-Russia-US summit have sent a clear message: the Taiwan question is at the heart of China's core interests and the international community's commitment to the one-China principle is unshakable, experts and scholars across the Taiwan Strait said.
They said the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces and military buildup are doomed to fail.
On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping met with US President Donald Trump, who was in the southern Chinese metropolis of Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. Xi also hosted a historic summit with Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the same day.
During his meeting with Trump, Xi said that on the Taiwan question, the US side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-US relations. Trump, for his part, said the United States does not support "Taiwan independence."
Chen Guiqing, a research fellow at the Beijing-based Institute of Taiwan Studies, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi had once again made China's firm position on the Taiwan question clear to the United States while also setting out China's expectations.
The Taiwan question concerns not only the overall stability of China-US relations but also global stability, Chen said. Doing the right thing means, among other things, that the United States should stop playing the "Taiwan card" and refrain from sending wrong signals to secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," he said. Otherwise, it will affect efforts by the two countries to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability, Chen added.
Ni Yongjie, director of the Shanghai Institute of Taiwan Studies, noted that this was the first time during Trump's presidency that he had publicly stated at a meeting between the two heads of state that the United States does not support "Taiwan independence."
The statement represented a response by the US side to China's major concerns over the Taiwan question, Ni said.
Experts said the Taiwan-related positions articulated by the two leaders dealt another heavy blow to secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence."
Chang Chun-kai, a research fellow at the Center for Cross-Strait Political and Economic Studies, Chengchi University, said the one-China principle constitutes the political foundation of China-US relations and is indispensable to ensuring peace and stability.
Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait depend on the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, Chang said, adding that this is also in line with the broader trend toward a stable relationship between China and the United States.
The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC.
The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed.
At the trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump, Xi stressed that countries should not interfere in one another's domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said.
Putin said the three countries should adhere to the principles of sovereign equality and noninterference in internal affairs, and look for ways to resolve concerns in a balanced manner through cooperation.
Li Huan, a research fellow at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations, said the summit carries an important message for the Taiwan question: major countries are willing to sit down and communicate directly to manage differences and avoid misjudgment and conflict, which shatters the attempt and illusion of secessionist forces to exploit competition among major countries to pursue "Taiwan independence."
Commenting on Trump's statement and the consensus reached by the three heads of state, Chen said that although secessionist forces on the island are trying to downplay their significance, more and more people in Taiwan will come to see clearly that "Taiwan independence" attempts find no support and will never succeed.
Xi noted at the summit that, as the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defend the hard-won outcomes of victory in World War II.
Li said Taiwan's restoration to China was one of the outcomes of victory in World War II and an important part of the postwar international order, adding that the historical and legal fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China is clear and indisputable.
By recalling the three countries' history of fighting side by side during World War II and reaffirming their commitment to safeguarding the postwar international order and the purposes of the UN Charter, the summit sent a stern warning to forces seeking to challenge that order and undermine the achievements of the war, including secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," she said.
Feng Wang, a Taiwan-based history writer, said the history of World War II and the victory over fascism were shared historical memories of the international community that must neither be forgotten nor distorted.
People in Taiwan should not be misled by political manipulation or erroneous views of history, Wang said, adding that people from all walks of life in Taiwan should take a long-term and broad view, thinking in the direction that benefits Taiwan compatriots, the country and the Chinese nation.
"Secession aimed at 'Taiwan independence' is the root cause of turmoil across the Taiwan Strait. It harms the immediate interests of the people on both sides of the strait and is widely opposed by the international community. It is a dead end," Ni said.
The DPP authorities should abandon their secessionist stance as soon as possible and return to the path of peaceful development of cross-strait relations, he added.

articles.title: New era for math? AI helps prove the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis
articles.titleCn: 数学新时代？AI助力证明167年历史的黎曼猜想
articles.summary: New era for math? AI helps prove the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis
articles.summaryCn: Anthropic数学家Levent Alpöge宣布与AI模型Claude合作证明了167年历史的黎曼猜想，引发数学界关于AI辅助证明意义的热议。

paragraphs.en: A {{0}} claim had the math world buzzing this weekend. Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, announced that he had worked with the company's AI model Claude to produce a proof of the 167-year-old Riemann {{1}}. "This is a great contribution. You could say it has shaken the world and marked the beginning of a new era in mathematics," Fields Medalist Shing-Tung Yau, dean of Tsinghua University's Qiuzhen College, said on Saturday evening. Proposed in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, the hypothesis concerns the {{2}} of prime numbers.
paragraphs.cn: 一个爆炸性声明让这个周末的数学界沸腾了。人工智能公司Anthropic的数学家Levent Alpöge宣布，他与该公司的AI模型Claude合作，给出了167年历史的黎曼猜想的证明。菲尔兹奖得主、清华大学求真书院院长丘成桐周六晚间表示：“这是一个伟大的贡献。可以说它震撼了世界，标志着数学新时代的开始。”该猜想由德国数学家波恩哈德·黎曼于1859年提出，涉及素数的分布。

paragraphs.en: Primes, such as 2, 3, 5 and 7, are natural numbers greater than 1 that are {{3}} only by 1 and themselves. The hypothesis points to an {{4}} mathematical pattern in their {{5}} random distribution along the number line. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1 million prize for a correct solution. articles.fullText:
A bombshell claim had the math world buzzing this weekend. Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, announced that he had worked with the company's AI model Claude to produce a proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis.
"This is a great contribution. You could say it has shaken the world and marked the beginning of a new era in mathematics," Fields Medalist Shing-Tung Yau, dean of Tsinghua University's Qiuzhen College, said on Saturday evening.
Proposed in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers. Primes, such as 2, 3, 5 and 7, are natural numbers greater than 1 that are divisible only by 1 and themselves. The hypothesis points to an underlying mathematical pattern in their seemingly random distribution along the number line. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1 million prize for a correct solution. A proof would have far-reaching implications across mathematics and could also have implications in fields such as cryptography and physics.
Alpöge made the announcement on Friday, releasing more than 17 million lines of code written in Lean, a programming language in which a computer checks every step of a proof. He said Claude had also generated a written draft running to more than 250,000 pages, which he held back because it was too unwieldy to read. Alpöge said he did not yet fully understand all the mathematics in the argument.
A day later, the Lean and Mathlib communities said in a joint statement that Alpöge's Riemann hypothesis proof had passed community verification.
The work has sparked debate among mathematicians worldwide over what an AI-assisted proof would mean for the field and how it might change the way research is done.
"The page count doesn't matter. What matters is readability and no one can read 250,000 pages," Fields Medalist Deng Yu, a professor of mathematics at the University of Chicago, said on Saturday. He said a more readable version might emerge soon and that he would reserve judgment until then.
Fields Medalist Shing-Tung Yau speaks on stage, Beijing, March 28, 2025. 
"AI will become an indispensable part of our research," Yau said. "As for human ingenuity, I think machines still have a long way to go." He said AI was far better at solving problems than at posing them. In his view, asking questions takes more creativity and the key is knowing which questions matter.
"If you know a theorem is true, you can use it. If you understand why it's true, you can try applying the same method to problems we still haven't solved," said Artan Sheshmani, a researcher at the Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications. He said he wanted to understand what mathematical principle made the Riemann hypothesis true, assuming the proof holds up, and where else that principle might apply.
Alpöge's account also offered a glimpse of Claude's role in shaping the argument. He said a simpler mathematical problem had led him to explore a new approach. Later, Claude suggested how many times to repeat a key mathematical operation. Sheshmani saw that as a creative contribution. AI can surprise experts with an idea and explore where it leads, he said, while Lean checks the logic. Mathematicians still have to decide what is worth studying, interpret the findings and take responsibility for the conclusions they make public.
The logo of Anthropic. 
Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, a day before Alpöge's announcement. The timing prompted speculation about whether the release was intended to generate publicity. Alpöge himself described the timing as "terrible."

articles.fullText:
(ECNS) -- China's Supreme People's Court and the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese jointly released five typical cases on Monday, highlighting efforts to protect the lawful rights and interests of overseas Chinese, returned overseas Chinese and their families.
The cases focus on strengthening cooperation between courts and overseas Chinese organizations, ensuring equal protection under the law, improving dispute resolution mechanisms and fostering a law-based business environment, according to the Supreme People's Court.
The first case involved a property dispute in Xiamen, in east China's Fujian Province, that had lasted more than a decade. The dispute centered on a century-old house inherited by overseas Chinese but occupied by a tenant's family for more than 70 years. Through coordination among the court, overseas Chinese organizations and local authorities, the parties reached a comprehensive mediation agreement, resolving the longstanding dispute.
The second case involved an international sales contract dispute between companies in Chile and Vietnam. The Vietnamese company delivered goods worth $627,000, but the Chilean company paid only $339,000, citing quality concerns.
After the debt was transferred to an overseas Chinese claimant, the claimant filed a lawsuit in Qingtian County, in east China's Zhejiang Province, seeking about $460,000 in payment and related charges. The court worked with overseas Chinese organizations and trade promotion experts to facilitate mediation and resolve the dispute.
The third case involved an overseas Chinese-invested enterprise in Huangshan, in east China's Anhui Province, seeking to recover more than 380,000 yuan (about $53,000) in unpaid bills from a company in Dongguan, in south China's Guangdong Province. Through property preservation measures and mediation, the court helped the enterprise recover the full outstanding amount.
In the fourth case, a state-owned overseas Chinese farm in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region was ordered to repay more than 5 million yuan in a lease contract dispute.
Rather than immediately freezing the farm's operating accounts or auctioning its assets, the court adopted flexible enforcement measures to minimize disruption to its business operations. The parties eventually reached a settlement, and the farm repaid its debts ahead of schedule.
The fifth case involved a service contract dispute between a pharmaceutical research company and an overseas Chinese-invested biopharmaceutical company. After mediation by the Shanghai Commercial Mediation Center, the parties agreed on payment of outstanding service fees. The Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court later confirmed that the mediation agreement was legally valid.
The Supreme People's Court said the cases demonstrate the importance of coordinated dispute resolution, appropriate judicial measures and equal protection of lawful rights and interests. Such efforts are expected to improve the handling of disputes involving overseas Chinese and support a fair, transparent and predictable business environment.

articles.fullText:
China has drilled a high-yield gas well in volcanic rock formations at a depth of more than 5,000 meters in the central Bohai Sea, marking a major breakthrough in offshore ultra-deep natural gas exploration.
The well was drilled on Thursday to a depth of 5,770 meters and tested at a daily gas output of approximately 800,000 cubic meters.
During exploration, the well encountered more than 120 meters of gas-bearing formations in volcanic rock, demonstrating the vast exploration potential of offshore ultra-deep volcanic rock reservoirs.
Guo Tao, chief geologist at the Bohai Petroleum Research Institute of CNOOC Tianjin, said the reservoir temperature reached 150 degrees Celsius, while formation pressure exceeded 80 megapascals.
Facing challenging high-temperature and high-pressure geological conditions, teams from multiple disciplines worked together to improve operational quality under complex geological conditions, ultimately completing the drilling operation and obtaining a high-yield gas flow.
In offshore oil and gas exploration, formations buried deeper than 3,500 meters are generally classified as deep, while those exceeding 4,500 meters are considered ultra-deep.
The ultra-deep volcanic rocks in the Bohai Sea were formed by volcanic eruptions and subsequently underwent multiple phases of tectonic transformation. Their dense lithology and strong heterogeneity have made exploration particularly challenging.
Difficulty in accurately identifying complex formations, locating high-quality reservoirs and drilling through hard rock has long posed world-class technical challenges to exploration and development in the area.
The Bohai Sea is a major natural gas production region in China and an important source of gas supply for Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and surrounding areas.
The successful drilling of the well opens up a new frontier for China's offshore ultra-deep natural gas exploration. It is expected to accelerate exploration in the ultra-deep Bohai region and support the development of a giant gas province with reserves of one trillion cubic meters.
The breakthrough also carries significance for increasing domestic oil and gas reserves and production, while ensuring a stable natural gas supply to regional markets.

中国在渤海中部水深超过5000米的火山岩地层中钻获一口高产天然气井，标志着海上超深天然气勘探取得重大突破。该井于周四钻至5770米深度，测试日产天然气约80万立方米。勘探过程中，该井在火山岩中钻遇超过120米的气层，展示了海上超深火山岩储层巨大的勘探潜力。中海油天津渤海石油研究院首席地质学家郭涛表示，储层温度达到150摄氏度，地层压力超过80兆帕。面对高温高压的复杂地质条件挑战，多学科团队协同合作，在复杂地质条件下提高作业质量，最终完成钻井作业并获得高产气流。在海上油气勘探中，埋深超过3500米的地层通常被归类为深层，而超过4500米的则被视为超深层。

渤海超深火山岩由火山喷发形成，随后经历了多期构造改造。其岩性致密、非均质性强，使勘探尤为困难。准确识别复杂地层、定位优质储层以及钻穿坚硬岩石的困难，长期以来对该地区的勘探开发构成了世界级技术挑战。渤海是中国主要的天然气产区，也是京津冀及周边地区重要的天然气供应来源。该井的成功钻探为中国海上超深天然气勘探开辟了新领域。预计将加速渤海超深区域的勘探，并支持建设储量达一万亿立方米的巨型气区。
